subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Cry, the Beloved Country and Apartheid
description: A quick, practical guide to Cry, the Beloved Country and Apartheid.

hook.text: Alan Paton wrote a novel about South Africa that was published the same year apartheid became law.

buildup.text: Cry, the Beloved Country followed a Black pastor searching for his son in crime-ridden Johannesburg.

discovery.text: Published in 1948, the novel became an international bestseller and turned global eyes on South Africa.

twist.text: The apartheid government confiscated Paton's passport to prevent him from speaking abroad.

climax.text: The novel built international sympathy that would eventually fuel the anti-apartheid movement worldwide.

punchline.text: A silenced author's words traveled further than he could.

quiz.question: How did the apartheid government respond to Alan Paton?
options: They awarded him a national prize
They confiscated his passport to silence him
They translated his book into Afrikaans
